F21 Relationship to host platform

Host platform

F21.host-platform The platform this surface runs on.

● supported

Value: Cursor is based upon the VS Code codebase. It is regularly rebased onto the latest VS Code version, and often uses slightly older VS Code versions for stability.

F01 Loop and built-in tools

Loop shape

F01.loop-shape How a turn runs: plan, tool call, result, stop.

● supported

Value: The agent works through a series of tool calls, deciding what to do next based on the result of each action. It uses tools to search code, edit files, and run the terminal, then reads each result before its next step. A stop hook is called when the agent loop ends and can optionally auto-submit a follow-up user message to keep iterating.

Evidence:

  • E-cursor-01439

    [tools in a loop](https://cursor.com/learn/agents.md): instead of always returning a single answer, it works through a series of tool calls, deciding what to do next based on the result of each action. F02 Context and memory

Context window size

F02.context-window-size Window sizes available and how to choose one.

◐ partial

Value: Cloud Agents let you select the context window size; a larger window can increase token usage and costs. A subagent model string such as claude-opus-5[context=300k] sets the context window to 300k tokens. On request-based plans, Max Mode enables larger context windows.

Limitation: Automations use each model's maximum supported context window because they run as cloud agents. There is no context-window toggle.

Automatic compaction

F02.auto-compaction When and how history is summarized without a command.

● supported ! unverified [unverified: no verified evidence record; settles by A tester pass of this supported cell against its cited quotes. It was outside the 30% verification sample.]

Value: When the context window gets close to full, Cursor compresses older parts of the conversation into a summary to leave more room for new conversation. The preCompact hook is called before compaction and is observational: it cannot block or modify the compaction behavior.

Evidence:

  • E-cursor-00061

    Every chat shares a fixed context window with the model. As you add files, run tools, and exchange messages, those tokens fill up. When the window gets close to full, Cursor compresses older parts of the conversation into a summary to leave more room for new conversation.

    Source: https://cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

  • E-cursor-00909

    Called before context window compaction/summarization occurs. This is an observational hook that cannot block or modify the compaction behavior. Useful for logging when compaction happens or notifying users.

    Source: https://cursor.com/docs/hooks.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

Persistent memory

F02.persistent-memory Memory that survives sessions: files, notes or an auto-memory store.

● supported ! unverified [unverified: no verified evidence record; settles by A tester pass of this supported cell against its cited quotes. It was outside the 30% verification sample.]

Precedence and scoping

F03.precedence-scoping Which file wins and how directories nest.

● supported

Value: Team Rules work alongside other rule types and take precedence. Bugbot merges its rules in the order Team Rules, project .cursor/BUGBOT.md (including nested files), learned rules, manual rules. The closest applicable APPROVAL_POLICY.md has the highest priority for files under its directory; ancestor policies still apply unless they conflict.

F06.output-blocking Exit codes or JSON that allow, deny, ask or modify.

● supported

Value: Exit code 0 means the hook succeeded and its JSON output is used; exit code 2 blocks the action, equivalent to returning permission: deny. The nested permissionDecision and updatedInput map to permission and updated_input. failClosed can be set for critical hooks.

◐ partial

Value: The SDK tools option allowlists the built-in tools offered to the model, and disallowed_tools removes tools and keeps the rest. Subagents can be configured with custom prompts, tool access, and models.

Nesting rules

F09.nesting-rules Whether and how deep agents can spawn agents.

◐ partial

Value: Since Cursor 2.5, subagents can launch child subagents within a nesting limit, forming a tree of coordinated work. The main agent and its direct subagents can launch subagents. The Python SDK docs state the same rule.

Limitation: A subagent launched by another subagent can't launch further ones (E-cursor-01432). Side chats: 'Nesting is not supported. A side chat cannot spawn its own side chats.' (E-cursor-04224)

  • E-cursor-01432

    Yes, within a nesting limit. Since Cursor 2.5, subagents can launch child subagents to create a tree of coordinated work. The main agent and its direct subagents can launch subagents, but a subagent launched by another subagent can't launch further ones.

    Source: https://cursor.com/docs/subagents.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

  • E-cursor-01182

    reaches the same subagent executor the parent has, so a parent can delegate to a subagent that delegates further. Each level sees the same set of named subagents. The top-level agent and its direct subagents can launch subagents, but a subagent launched by another subagent can't launch further ones.

Mode defaults and persistence

F19.mode-defaults The default mode and whether a choice persists.

● supported

Value: Agent is the default mode (no --mode value needed in the CLI; the SDK AgentOptions mode defaults to agent). On follow-up SDK sends, omitting mode keeps the conversation's current mode; passing mode switches for that run only. Each mode uses its own context, so switching modes starts a fresh context window.
